title: How much slack is in the triangle inequality?

prereqs.why: Every one of the three distances is a count of disagreeing positions.
The quantity asked for is the slack in the triangle inequality, so its sign is the thing the axiom promises.

statement:
On $X = \{0,1\}^8$ the **Hamming distance** $d_H(x,y)$ is the number of
positions at which $x$ and $y$ differ.

Take

$$\begin{aligned}
x &= 0\,1\,1\,0\,1\,0\,0\,1\\
y &= 1\,1\,0\,1\,1\,0\,0\,0\\
z &= 1\,0\,1\,1\,0\,0\,1\,1
\end{aligned}$$

Work out

$$d_H(x,y) + d_H(y,z) - d_H(x,z).$$
hints: Line the strings up one under another and mark the columns where the two you are comparing disagree. Three comparisons, eight columns each.
The triangle inequality says the answer cannot be negative. If you get a negative number, one of the three counts is wrong.
Count $d_H(x,y)$ first: the strings agree in positions 2, 5, 6 and 7, so they disagree in the other four.

payload.label: The slack
payload.syntax: A whole number. Arithmetic is fine: 4+5-5 is read as 4.
